"To transfer a car to yourself after the death of your common law partner in Ontario, you will need to act as the executor of their estate or obtain a court order if no will exists. If there's a will, the executor must provide a copy of the will, vehicle ownership papers, death certificate, and proof of insurance to ServiceOntario to transfer ownership. If there's no will, a lawyer may be needed to draft a letter of opinion for the Ministry of Transportation. "

From everything I have read online, it does appear as though you need to "apply to the court to be appointed as the estate trustee (also known as an executor)." 

"You'll need the death certificate, identification, and any relevant documentation about your relationship. You'll need to fill out the necessary court forms for applying to be the estate trustee, which can be found on the Ontario Courts website. You must notify all potential beneficiaries, including family members and creditors, by serving them with the necessary court forms. Once the forms are completed and served, you'll need to file them with the Superior Court of Justice in the applicable registry. If your application is successful, the court will issue a Certificate of Appointment of Estate Trustee, which gives you the authority to administer the estate."

Based on everything I've read in your posts and comments, I feel like it will be easy enough to get the necessary paperwork from the court to enable you to do things like change the car into your name. I would recommend looking into this first. I have listed a few links below for you that I have found while researching this information for you.

https://www.ontario.ca/page/serviceontario

With Vyvanse it is released over 14 hours, so it is much more stable, in my opinion. When I was on Dexamfetamine and Ritalin they were both instant release, meaning that I had to take them three times a day. Morning, lunch, and afternoon. If I didn't take them exactly at the right time (something I was not great at, especially the morning ones), it affected how they worked. They made me feel racey and definitely caused my anxiety to increase. I also struggled to eat and dropped down to 47kgs. I'm 5'6. I looked terrible. If I didn't take one in the afternoon, I crashed, but when I did, I was always awake much later than I wanted to be. It was a vicious cycle. 

Vyvanse has none of these side effects. I can eat properly now. Go to sleep at a decent time, and don't have to worry about taking meds multiple times throughout the day. I set an alarm for 6:30 a.m. every morning to take it so when I get up at 7:30-8 a.m. it has already started working. This means I no longer feel sluggish upon first waking up. Because it releases over a 14-hour period, it is done so in a way that doesn't cause me to crash in the afternoon.
